description: Proxy credentials disclosed in ERR_PROXY_INVALID_CONFIG error messages (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-48615)
overview: Node.js discloses proxy credentials in `ERR_PROXY_INVALID_CONFIG` error messages. CVE-2026-48615 established that a proxy credential must not appear in a Node.js error message and redacted the username and password from `ProxyConfig.href`, but that fix missed four error paths in the same subsystem, one of them inside the same constructor, which interpolate the raw proxy URL, credentials included, into an `ERR_PROXY_INVALID_CONFIG` message. The proxy URL comes from the environment, but the defect is the sink: a secret that Node.js redacts everywhere else is emitted verbatim into a much wider audience than the process environment, such as stderr, container logs, log aggregation, and crash reporting services. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
